transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Martin (Redwood SE), Priya (Helix Head of Eng), Liam (Platform Lead), Eva (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete):
- Helix evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for payments fraud/cc detection assistant.
- Main integration questions: SDK support (python/node), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy pattern, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks and tracing, and security (KMS, audit logs, SSO).
- Agreed to run a PoC baseline to validate latency and cost; Redwood to share pricing and integration samples.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Martin our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:05] Priya: Hi, thanks for doing this. I'm Priya, head of engineering at Helix. We have Liam and Eva on from platform and security.
[00:10] Liam: Hey all.
[00:12] Martin: Hi, quick agenda from our side: understand your stack, integration constraints, and what success looks like for a PoC. We'll go into SDKs and sample flows, and then call out next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Priya: Yep, perfect. To start, quick background: we're a payments platform, we process authorizations and some downstream reconciliation, and want to add an assistant and retrievers for internal ops and risk. Low latency for realtime decisions is important, and PII rules mean we may need Private or VPC.
[00:35] Eva: Security is top of mind: SOC2 is a baseline, we have strict key ownership requirements, and we need audit logs + SSO/SAML. Also data residency in EU for some customers.
[00:45] Sofia: Great — that's inline with a lot of customers. A quick question on expected load: Priya, ballpark QPS and peak concurrency for the model calls?
[00:52] Priya: For the assistant front-end it's modest, maybe 5-10 qps normal, spikes to 80-100 qps during batch runs. For the realtime fraud check path we expect sub-200ms tail latency target and about 200 qps at peak for a pilot.
[01:05] Martin: Helpful. So two workloads: lower-throughput conversational + higher-throughput realtime gating. For realtime we often recommend Dedicated or a Private deployment with pinned capacity to meet tail SLOs. Hosted can work with autoscaling but there are tradeoffs on cold start and tail.
[01:20] Liam: Are there SDKs for our stack? We're mostly Node microservices and some Python workers. We often use LangChain in a few orchestrators, and LlamaIndex for vector retrieval pipelines.
[01:30] Sofia: Yes: we have official SDKs for python and node, plus OpenAI-compatible REST surface. For LangChain and LlamaIndex we provide connector examples; Martin can share specific snippet files.
[01:40] Martin: I'll drop concrete LangChain connector code. For LlamaIndex we show retrieval + embeddings flow and how to plug in our embeddings endpoint. Also show how to keep an API gateway/proxy in front for tenant routing and to enforce rate limits.
[01:55] Priya: About the gateway — we already have an edge proxy which does auth and routing. We want to route some calls to hosted Redwood but route higher-risk flows to Dedicated or to our VPC. How doable is that?
[02:08] Martin: That's a common pattern. You can run a tenant-aware gateway that sets model/route headers. Redwood supports policy-based routing: route by latency or by tag, and we have automatic fallback to compatible model variants. For VPC/private, you can deploy a private control plane and push inference into your network.
[02:25] Eva: On encryption — we need customer-managed keys. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[02:30] Sofia: Yes, Private and Dedicated offer KMS integrations. For Hosted we have envelope encryption and can support BYOK KMS for enterprise customers, with audit logs. We'll share the network diagram and KMS note.
[02:40] Priya: Rate limits — we have synchronous fraud checks that mustn't be throttled. We want to set per-route quotas and ensure retries don't overwhelm systems. How are rate limits represented? Token-based? Request-per-second?
[02:52] Martin: We support both per-route RPS and token budgets. For generation workloads we expose token-cost metrics; you can set per-API-key quotas or per-route policies. Our SDK exposes headers with quota usage and estimated token cost so you can pre-check.
[03:10] Liam: Observability hooks — we need traces and spans for requests end-to-end. Does Redwood support OpenTelemetry and trace context propagation?
[03:18] Martin: Yes, we support trace context propagation, and you can forward spans to your observability backend. We also provide per-request metadata in logs (model, sequence length, cache hit/miss, latency percentiles). You can stream these to S3 or a SIEM.
[03:33] Priya: For caching — our retriever uses a prefix KV cache for embeddings; curious how Redwood's KV cache and batching help with unit cost.
[03:42] Sofia: Our runtime does automatic prefix and KV caching where applicable. For embeddings, we also recommend local caching at the app level plus Redwood's memoization for repeated prompts. That significantly reduces per-token cost.
[03:55] Eva: Compliance-wise we need SOC2 report, ISO, and some pen test results. Also data retention controls.
[04:02] Sofia: We'll share our SOC2 summary, audit logs docs, and retention controls. For Private deployments you keep control of logs; for Hosted there's retention configuration and export hooks.
[04:15] Priya: Ok. About integration complexity: how much effort to wire LangChain/LlamaIndex? We're already using LangChain but not heavily.
[04:24] Martin: Very low — usually a few hours to wire the connector and auth. For LlamaIndex retrieval pipeline, you'll need to switch embeddings endpoint and set batching parameters. We'll provide a sample repo.
[04:36] Liam: How about local testing and a gateway/proxy sample? We want a dev loop to run against Hosted first, then switch to Dedicated.
[04:44] Martin: We have a local proxy example that simulates tenant routing and can toggle routing rules. We'll include a Dockerized sample.
[04:52] Priya: Pricing — we need a Hosted vs Dedicated comparison for predictable costs and tail latency guarantees. Also Dedicated reserved capacity options.
[04:59] Sofia: I'll shoot over a spreadsheet with estimated costs for your projected QPS and token volumes, plus TCO for Dedicated with 6/12 month commits. For Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets.
[05:10] Eva: Any red flags around data egress or PCI? We process payment data but tokenization removes PANs before it's sent. Still want assurances on not storing sensitive fields.
[05:20] Martin: We recommend redaction at the app edge; Redwood has data controls to prevent retention and to scrub tokens. For PCI-sensitive pieces we suggest Private or VPC with customer-managed keys.
[05:30] Priya: Timeline: We're aiming for a pilot in about 2 weeks if integration looks straightforward. Can Redwood support a quick PoC with baseline tests?
[05:38] Sofia: Yes — we can set up a PoC. Next step we'll define baseline test plan (QPS, latency percentiles, payload sizes) and run a short benchmark.
[05:48] Liam: Who will own the PoC on Redwood side?
[05:50] Sofia: Martin will lead on the SE side, I'll coordinate pricing and contract.
[05:55] Eva: We'll need security paperwork reviewed before any shared keys.
[05:58] Sofia: Understood. We'll attach SOC2 and network diagrams to the follow-up.
[06:03] Priya: Sounds good.
[06:06] Sofia: Quick recap: Redwood to send pricing + benchmark sheet, Martin to share LangChain/LlamaIndex code examples and gateway/proxy sample, Helix to share QPS and SLOs, and security to confirm KMS/retention requirements. Schedule follow-up PoC kickoff for week of 2026-03-30.
[06:22] Priya: Yep, thanks everyone.
[06:25] Sofia: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
